A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TG/NAE study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G are readable and can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original reading-time prediction experiments, model comparisons, ablations, and supplementary analyses, including Tables 1–3 and 6–8.

after.justification: v2 reports updated original reading-time prediction results and retains the main and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The architectures, training objectives, COMPOSE/STACK mechanisms, NAE aggregation procedure, and parallel-parsing approach are retained. Corrected formulas and clearer token indexing do not establish a change to the implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions train on BLLIP-LG and evaluate English self-paced reading times from Natural Stories. The corrected dataset release retains the same task and population coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Transformer, TG−comp, and CLT. The appendix comparisons also retain their comparator membership; RNNG remains the parser used to generate alternative structures.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 switches to a Natural Stories release explicitly described as correcting data misalignment, revising the evaluation data underlying the central reading-time analyses. Retained observations change from 724,883 to 725,875. Training budgets, filtering rules, regression controls, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The COMPOSE ablation and POS analyses retain their designs but provide substantially revised evidence: TG−comp's unique contribution under the full controls disappears, and its former POS-specific advantages disappear or reverse (Section 5.1, Figure 4). The CLT control and supplementary experiments remain present with updated results.

E5.justification: Table 2 changes its stated p-value-summary scope from across random seeds to seeds achieving significance. The three-seed design, means and standard deviations, significant-seed counts, standard errors, and statistical tests are otherwise retained.

E6.justification: Table 1's TG/Transformer ΔLogLik values change from 96.3/35.2 to 76.6/42.8. TG−comp's unique-contribution test in Section 5.1 changes from p<0.001 to p=0.478. POS findings and Tables 3 and 6–8 also change substantially. These updated results use corrected evaluation data, preventing interpretation as same-setting model performance changes.

T1.justification: Equation 1 restores the missing negative sign in normalized entropy and explicitly defines the preceding-position set. Equation 2 corrects a sum to the product required by the probability chain rule. These are localized mathematical corrections.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims that TG's attention predicts reading times better than Transformer's, that both contribute independently, and that the findings support complementary syntactic and token memory representations.

C2.justification: Transformer's advantage is reinterpreted through noun-triggered semantic retrieval rather than possessive-pronoun antecedent retrieval. Section 5.1 replaces the strategic retrieval of constituents within composed phrases with an emphasis on COMPOSE's role in verb retrieval. v2 also qualifies the algorithmic-level positioning and explains Appendix F's dependence on excluding Transformer's NAE.

D1.justification: v2 adds a reproduction-code link, identifies the corrected Natural Stories release, and clarifies top-layer NAE calculation and word-to-token indexing in Appendix D. Hyperparameters, hardware, computational cost, and software-version disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: References are added for interference, spillover, regression testing, and parsing assumptions, including Nicenboim et al. (2018), Van Dyke and McElree (2011), and Wurm and Fisicaro (2014). The central positioning around cue-based retrieval and syntactic memory remains, with a more qualified algorithmic-level comparison.

P1.justification: v2 separates cue-based retrieval into its own background subsection, expands the dataset-selection rationale, refines word/token terminology, and updates affiliations and acknowledgments. The main section sequence and Appendices A–G remain, with Appendix F retitled.

P2.justification: Figures 2–4 have revised axis ranges, POS categories, or legends, and Figure 4 gains a significance explanation. Table 2 and several appendix tables move. The figure/table inventory and overall two-column presentation remain.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses a central data-validity problem by using the corrected Natural Stories release and updating the main and appendix results and interpretations accordingly. This materially strengthens the empirical foundation, including revising the COMPOSE account when its earlier evidence no longer holds. Corrected mathematical formulas, reproduction-code access, and more qualified theoretical positioning provide additional gains.
